body: Constructive feedback is crucial for creative writers to refine their storytelling abilities. Since receiving feedback from human experts is often costly and time-intensive, large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable and efficient alternative as automatic writing assistants. Despite their potential, research indicates that LLM-generated feedback is often generic, lacks actionability, and fails to identify which writing issue is most critical. To address these limitations, we present a reinforcement learning approach that steers LLMs to generate constructive feedback without the need for ground-truth feedback. We train our model using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) with a novel multi-component reward function aiming at constructiveness: it prioritizes feedback that is uniquely tailored to the story, helps to improve story quality, and addresses the most critical writing issue. In automatic and human evaluation across three story corpora, our approach outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs (including Gemini) and competitive baselines. We find that providing actionable suggestions is the main driver of feedback constructiveness.
summaryZh: 该研究提出了一种利用强化学习（RL）生成建设性故事反馈的方法，以克服当前大语言模型（LLMs）生成的反馈往往过于笼统、缺乏可操作性且未能识别关键问题的缺点。研究采用了一种名为GRPO（Group Relative Policy Optimization）的算法，并设计了一个多组件奖励函数，该函数优先考虑反馈的独特性、对故事质量的提升作用以及对最关键问题的解决。实验表明，该方法在自动和人工评估中均优于现有最先进模型，证明了提供可操作性建议是提升反馈建设性的关键。
